title: Applying for Citizenship
summary: What happens when you apply for citizenship, how to use this booklet to prepare, what the citizenship test covers and who must write it, and what to expect at the citizenship ceremony.

sections.title: Applying for Citizenship

blocks.text: When you apply for citizenship, officials will check your status, verify that you are not prohibited from applying, and ensure that you meet the requirements.
Your application may take several months. Please ensure that the Call Centre always has your correct address while your application is being processed.

sections.title: How to use this booklet to prepare for the citizenship test

blocks.text: This booklet will help you prepare for the citizenship test. You should:

items: Ask a friend or family member to help you practise answering questions about Canada;
Call a local school or school board, a college, a community centre or a local organization that provides services to immigrants and ask for information on citizenship classes;
Take English or French language classes, which the Government of Canada offers free of charge.

focus: Four ways to prepare: study this guide; practise with a friend or family member; ask about citizenship classes; take English or French language classes.
The Government of Canada offers English or French language classes free of charge.
For citizenship classes, call a local school or school board, a college, a community centre or a local organization that serves immigrants.

sections.title: About the citizenship test

blocks.text: The citizenship test is usually a written test, but it could be an interview. You will be tested on two basic requirements for citizenship: 1) knowledge of Canada and of the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, and 2) adequate knowledge of English or French. Adult applicants 55 years of age and over do not need to write the citizenship test.

The Citizenship Regulations provide information on how your ability to meet the knowledge of Canada requirement is determined. Information about this requirement can be found on page 64 of the study guide.
All the citizenship test questions are based on the subject areas noted in the Citizenship Regulations, and all required information is provided in this study guide.

sections.title: After the test

blocks.text: If you pass the test and meet all the other requirements, you will receive a Notice to Appear to Take the Oath of Citizenship. This document tells you the date, time and place of your citizenship ceremony.
If you do not pass the test, you will receive a notification indicating the next steps.
You are encouraged to bring your family and friends to celebrate this occasion.

focus: If you pass the test and meet all the other requirements, you receive a Notice to Appear to Take the Oath of Citizenship.
The Notice to Appear tells you the date, time and place of your citizenship ceremony.
At the ceremony you: take the Oath of Citizenship; sign the oath form; and receive your Canadian Citizenship Certificate.
If you do not pass the test, you receive a notification indicating the next steps.
You are encouraged to bring your family and friends to celebrate the ceremony.

quiz.q: When you apply for citizenship, what will officials do?
choices: Interview your friends and family members about your knowledge of Canada and its history
Give you your Canadian Citizenship Certificate right away and sign the oath form on your behalf
Enrol you in citizenship classes and in English or French language classes offered free of charge
Check your status, verify that you are not prohibited from applying, and ensure that you meet the requirements
quiz.why: The booklet says officials "will check your status, verify that you are not prohibited from applying, and ensure that you meet the requirements".

quiz.q: While your application is being processed, you must make sure the Call Centre always has your:
choices: Correct address
Passport number
Employer's name
Test results
quiz.why: "Please ensure that the Call Centre always has your correct address while your application is being processed."

quiz.q: Which of the following does the Government of Canada offer free of charge?
choices: Citizenship test coaching
Legal advice on immigration
English or French language classes
Travel to the citizenship ceremony
quiz.why: The booklet says to "take English or French language classes, which the Government of Canada offers free of charge".

quiz.q: Where does the booklet suggest you ask for information on citizenship classes?
choices: A local school or school board, a college, a community centre or a local organization that serves immigrants
The Call Centre, which must always have your correct address while your application is processed
The Government of Canada, which offers English or French language classes free of charge
The Citizenship Regulations, which provide information on the knowledge of Canada requirement
quiz.why: The booklet says to call "a local school or school board, a college, a community centre or a local organization that provides services to immigrants".

choices: An oral exam before a judge
A group discussion
An online quiz
A written test, but it could be an interview
quiz.why: "The citizenship test is usually a written test, but it could be an interview."

quiz.q: Which adult applicants do not need to write the citizenship test?
choices: Applicants 18 years of age and under
Applicants 65 years of age and over
Applicants 55 years of age and over
Applicants who speak both English and French
quiz.why: "Adult applicants 55 years of age and over do not need to write the citizenship test."

quiz.q: What are the two basic requirements for citizenship that you will be tested on?
choices: Knowledge of Canadian geography and history, and the ability to sign the oath form at the ceremony
Knowledge of Canada and of the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, and adequate knowledge of English or French
Knowledge of the Constitution and the Citizenship Regulations, and adequate knowledge of English or French
Knowledge of the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, and a correct address on file with the Call Centre
quiz.why: You are tested on "1) knowledge of Canada and of the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, and 2) adequate knowledge of English or French".

quiz.q: All the citizenship test questions are based on the subject areas noted in:
choices: The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
The Constitution of Canada
Magna Carta
The Citizenship Regulations
quiz.why: "All the citizenship test questions are based on the subject areas noted in the Citizenship Regulations."

quiz.q: If you pass the test and meet all the other requirements, you will receive:
choices: A Canadian passport
A Notice to Appear to Take the Oath of Citizenship
A Canadian Citizenship Certificate by mail
A letter from the Prime Minister
quiz.why: "If you pass the test and meet all the other requirements, you will receive a Notice to Appear to Take the Oath of Citizenship."

quiz.q: Which of the following will you do at the citizenship ceremony?
choices: Write the citizenship test
Apply for a passport
Receive your Canadian Citizenship Certificate
Register to vote
quiz.why: At the ceremony you take the Oath, sign the oath form, and "receive your Canadian Citizenship Certificate".

quiz.q: If you do not pass the citizenship test, you will:
choices: Have to leave Canada
Receive your Citizenship Certificate anyway
Be invited to the ceremony as a guest
Receive a notification indicating the next steps
quiz.why: "If you do not pass the test, you will receive a notification indicating the next steps."

quiz.q: What does the Notice to Appear to Take the Oath of Citizenship tell you?
choices: The result of your test and the next steps you must take
The questions you will be asked on the citizenship test
The date, time and place of your citizenship ceremony
The Call Centre telephone numbers for checking your application
quiz.why: "This document tells you the date, time and place of your citizenship ceremony."
